Subject: Invoice #INV-2026-048: Q4 True-up and Overage Clarification

Hi Marissa,

We received invoice INV-2026-048 for a one-time true-up/overage charge covering late-December usage. The amount is larger than we anticipated and our finance team is asking for a line-by-line breakdown showing which requests triggered overage billing versus committed capacity.

Context: we had a product launch on 2025-12-22 that generated a short burst of traffic across our EU and US regions. We expected this to fit within our reserved capacity (CommittedUnits) but the invoice suggests we exceeded the quarterly commitment by ~42k tokens and were billed at the on-demand rate.

Ask: can you provide (1) the per-day usage by region for 2025-12-20 through 2025-12-31, (2) the specific timestamps and request IDs that triggered billing outside the commitment, and (3) a proposed settlement — specifically whether Redwood will consider a one-time adjustment/credit given the burst was tied to a coordinated launch.

We'd like to avoid withholding payment, but we need the reconciliation before we can process the charge. Can you advise next steps and an ETA for the usage report?

Thanks,
Priya Narayan
Head of Engineering Operations
FinPay

Quick plan:
- Rohan will pull the usage exports and identify which requests were billed against on-demand vs committed capacity (ETA EOD tomorrow).
- Neha (billing) will prepare a draft reconciliation and propose an adjustment/credit option for review.
- I'll coordinate a short call if needed — are you available tomorrow 4pm PT / 7pm ET?

In the meantime, we can hold collection for this invoice while we reconcile; I will confirm with our finance team that we can pause the charge pending results. If that is acceptable to FinPay, please confirm and we'll mark the invoice on hold.

Action requested: Priya, please confirm if you want us to treat this as an urgent reconciliation (call today) or if email is fine.

Marissa / Priya — I pulled the initial export and did a quick scan for anomalies. Preliminary findings attached. Key points: 
- The spike on 2025-12-23 01:10:00 — 02:45:00 UTC shows sustained high-concurrency traffic routed to your dedicated pool but a subset of requests originated from eu-west-1 and were routed through our fallback pool in us-west-2 due to a transient cluster shift. Those requests were billed at on-demand rates.
- We also see several long-context sessions where the KV cache was not reused because of session id mismatch; those increased effective token counts.
- Total overage tokens (per our consumption model) for 2025-12-20..2025-12-31: 42,714 tokens. Region breakdown attached.

I've attached: usage_export_2025-12-20_2025-12-31.csv and redwood_prelim_notes_20260211.pdf (short explainer). I'll follow up with a cleaned per-request log if you need the raw IDs, but that will take a few hours.

Thanks,
Rohan Mehta
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

Hi Priya — thanks for flagging this. I ran the billing-side reconciliation based on Rohan's export and our billing system. Summary below and attached workbook with line-item math: true_up_calc_20260212.xlsx

Summary:
- Billed overage tokens: 42,714
- On-demand unit price: $0.0004 per token
- Raw overage charge: $17.0856 (system rounds to $17.09 on invoice)

Given the short-lived nature of the spike and that it stemmed from a routing anomaly during your launch, we're prepared to offer a goodwill settlement: a one-time credit equal to 30% of the raw overage charge (credit = $5.13). If FinPay accepts, we'll issue a credit memo, reissue the adjusted invoice, and mark the original invoice as disputed for collections purposes until the credit posts.

Proposed next steps:
1) FinPay confirms acceptance of the 30% credit (reply to this thread).
2) We produce final per-request logs for your audit within 48h.
3) We generate DocuSign paperwork for credit acceptance if you need a formal sign-off.

We can also escalate the credit amount if this needs leadership approval; I can loop in VP Finance.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Billing Operations Manager
